title: Safety collaborative prevention and control technology for coal mining beneath oil pipelines
content:
by Tuanjie Liu, Gui Liu, Xiangnan Li, Aiguo Guo, Yaokun Fu, Haoyu Hu

Coal mining beneath oil pipelines requires a balance between resource recovery and the control of mining-induced pipeline deformation. Using coal seam at Haichatan Coal Mine and the Jingbian-Yulin refined-oil pipeline as a case study, a coupled analysis framework was developed to link ground movement, relative pipe-soil displacement, and pipeline equivalent stress. The probability integral method was used to predict ground subsidence, tilt, horizontal strain, and curvature. The three-dimensional ground-displacement field was then applied to a nonlinear Winkler foundation model implemented in ANSYS. Sixteen scenarios were defined by combining two pipeline branches, two mining scales, and four mining-thickness levels. For full-thickness extraction of three panels, the maximum predicted ground subsidence along the western and eastern branches was 1 480 and 1 634 mm, respectively. The corresponding maximum pipeline equivalent stresses were 728 and 946 MPa, with strength-utilization ratios of 2.79 and 3.62. Reducing the effective mining thickness to 0.2M decreased these stresses to 255 and 227 MPa; however, the western branch remained close to the adopted limit, with a strength-utilization ratio of 0.977. Effective mining thickness strongly influenced the predicted response within the scenarios examined. A candidate control strategy combining a 2.3 m mining-thickness limit with trench excavation, pressure reduction, and pipeline lifting where necessary was proposed. Its safety requires further verification because the thickness limit alone does not establish compliance. A monitoring framework integrating InSAR, ground surveys, pipeline strain measurements, and trench-displacement measurements was also proposed to support model calibration and staged intervention. The framework provides a basis for assessing coal extraction beneath long-distance pipelines in areas with overlapping coal and petroleum resources.
